Claude & privacy MVP2 / foundation

Keys, history & deletion

Separate API key lifecycle, sanitized local history, and integration removal.

Development previewMVP2 foundation complete. Local service and the synthetic API demo work locally. Live hooks, enforcement, and Anthropic BYOK are pending.
On this pageCurrent invited beta scopeAPI keys belong in KeychainPrivate local historyDefault retentionThree separate operationsCloud and diagnostics

Current invited beta scope

This guide retains earlier milestone design and evidence. The current ten-tester beta preparation uses ad-hoc signatures and is not notarized. Production Cloud API deployment is verified; the signed native client connects through authenticated service IPC; genuine hosted inference and the complete native Claude review path have passed; broader evaluation remains in progress. Claude Code 2.1.290 callback allow/deny, timeout, outage and exact-action native human review checks pass using a local model double; Codex coverage remains unverified. Earlier pending statements describe their original milestone. No public download is published.

API keys belong in Keychain

The planned BYOK implementation stores its API key in macOS Keychain with appropriate login accessibility and signed-app-family access restrictions. The service reads the value only when required for an authenticated request.

Keys must not go into UserDefaults, SQLite, fixture JSON, logs, or the static website. The app needs distinct replace, validate, and delete operations with accurate errors and no full-key redisplay. Keychain integration is pending in the current build.

Private local history

The per-user service is the sole SQLite writer. Its implemented database path is ~/Library/Application Support/TraceRook/history.sqlite3, inside a 0700 directory with 0600 database, WAL, and shared-memory files. The store uses prepared statements, foreign keys, migrations, indexes, WAL, and transactional approval updates. Nullable subagent identities are normalized to prevent duplicate sessions.

Only sanitized event summaries and review metadata enter this store. Raw commands, transcripts, model bodies and credentials are excluded. Automated tests cover permissions, restart, bounded snapshots, retention, concurrent terminal transitions and history clearing. Simulated service ingestion is labeled and excluded from observed host-session counts.

Mock device credentials and API receipts stay in service memory; backend metadata is also ephemeral. These do not enter live SQLite or Keychain. Read local service evidence.

Default retention

DataDefaultNotes
Sanitized event summaries14 daysStartup purge implemented; daily scheduling and shorter settings pending
Incidents and approvals30 daysKeep explanations and decision audit
Session recordsUntil references expireRemove after retained events/incidents are gone
API keyUntil user deletes or replaces itKeychain; independent from history
Raw tool JSON / transcriptsDo not persist by defaultTemporary decision memory only

Durable retention, bounded queries and startup purge are implemented and tested. A periodic purge timer and configurable shorter retention remain pending. Offline fixture history and ephemeral mock API metadata are separate from live SQLite.

Three separate operations

  • Delete All Local History: remove retained session, event, finding, and approval records under a defined safe operation.
  • Delete API Key: remove the Keychain credential and make BYOK unavailable.
  • Uninstall Integrations: remove only TraceRook-owned hook entries and optionally unregister the helper.

Uninstalling an integration must not silently erase history or another agent’s settings. Deleting history must not imply deleting data Anthropic already received.

Cloud and diagnostics

Cloud Demo account and usage data are bundled samples. No real enrollment, billing record, or cloud history exists. Diagnostics exports are local and sanitized unless the user explicitly chooses a destination.

Local history settings and provider terms are separate privacy boundaries. See Anthropic consent and analysis and safe uninstall behavior.

Based on the MVP1 specification, the additive MVP2 specification, and the acceptance matrix · October 8, 2026.
